  • Lead discovery workshops to gather, define, and document current and future state business processes and functional requirements
  • Lead high-level integration discussions and design workshops and create current and future state architecture diagrams that you can relate to both technical and business-minded stakeholders which shows how Salesforce integrates with ERP and other systems
  • Develop robust, scalable and flexible solutions through the creation of architectural designs, prototypes, and proof-of-concepts and demonstrate solution functionality to client stakeholders
  • Act as the overall solution owner during the implementation phase ensuring the project’s scope and outcomes are on track
  • Conduct solution architecture reviews with project team members prior to design and development activities to ensure solution aligns to client requirements
  • Serve as the functional lead and coach team members to implement declarative configurations (Consultants) and customizations (Developers), jumping in to provide hands-on assistance when necessary
  • Demonstrate a strong understanding of Salesforce Revenue Cloud capabilities and clearly communicate its limitations and best practices to clients
  • Develop and present solution options to client, evaluating the pros and cons of declarative configuration against code and customization
  • Provide detailed level of effort estimates for proposed solutions. Articulate the benefits and risks to a solution’s feasibility and functionality
  • For clients with complex configuration requirements, you will leverage our strategic partner solution, Logik.io. Upon hire, we will train you to acquire a working knowledge of the Logik solution and during projects, you will be able to pull in our internal Logik.io Center of Excellence team

jobs.description:
Position:

Senior Cyber Defense Engineer


Job Description:

What You'll Be Doing:

Incident Response & Investigations

  • Lead complex cyber incident investigations across enterprise, cloud, hybrid, and on-premises environments.

  • Conduct end-to-end incident response activities including triage, scoping, containment, eradication, recovery, and post-incident reporting.

  • Investigate network intrusions, account compromise, ransomware, insider risk, fraud-related incidents, unauthorized access, and advanced threat actor activity.

  • Preserve evidence and maintain chain-of-custody procedures for forensic, legal, compliance, and regulatory investigations.

  • Produce clear investigative findings, root cause analysis, executive summaries, and remediation recommendations.

Digital Forensics & Malware Analysis

  • Perform DFIR activities across Windows, cloud, identity, endpoint, network, and application environments.

  • Conduct dead-box forensic examinations, artifact analysis, timeline analysis, and evidence collection.

  • Collect, analyze, and interpret host, network, cloud, email, identity, and application artifacts.

  • Analyze suspicious files, malware behavior, persistence mechanisms, attacker tooling, and indicators of compromise.

  • Support sensitive investigations involving Legal, HR, Compliance, Insider Risk, and business stakeholders.

Threat Hunting & Detection Engineering

  • Conduct proactive threat hunting to identify adversary behaviors, emerging threats, and control gaps.

  • Develop, tune, and improve SIEM detections, correlation rules, KQL queries, alerts, dashboards, and response workflows.

  • Apply MITRE ATT&CK, threat intelligence, incident lessons learned, and attacker TTPs to improve detection coverage.

  • Partner with SOC, Threat Intelligence, Engineering, and Platform teams to validate visibility and improve response outcomes.

  • Support continuous improvement of threat detection, alert quality, incident workflows, and security monitoring use cases.

Security Engineering & Platform Support

  • Support the engineering, administration, and optimization of cyber security tools and platforms.

  • Assist with log source onboarding, data normalization, telemetry validation, and use-case development.

  • Partner with Infrastructure, Cloud, Identity, Application, and Security Operations teams to improve visibility and response capability.

  • Build scripts, queries, automation, dashboards, and technical workflows that improve investigation speed and quality.

  • Help mature enterprise security capabilities across SIEM, EDR, NDR, SOAR, cloud security, identity security, and forensic tooling.

AI, Security Automation & Emerging Technologies

  • Use AI-assisted tools, copilots, automation, and scripting to improve investigation efficiency, reporting, and analysis.

  • Demonstrate curiosity and willingness to learn emerging AI, automation, and agent-assisted security operations capabilities.

  • Contribute to team initiatives involving AI-assisted workflows, personal security agents, team-developed agents, and operational automation.

  • Show evidence of hands-on experimentation through lab work, scripting, automation, prompt testing, AI tools, or practical tinkering.

  • Understand the security considerations of AI usage, including data protection, responsible use, prompt safety, and operational governance.

Threat Emulation, Red Teaming & Purple Team Support, Preferred

  • Apply an offensive security mindset during investigations to better understand attacker behavior, objectives, and tradecraft.

  • Support threat emulation and purple team activities that validate detections, controls, and response procedures.

  • Use knowledge of penetration testing, red teaming, adversary simulation, or ethical hacking to strengthen blue team defenses.

  • Assist with threat actor tracking, attack path analysis, lateral movement analysis, persistence review, and detection validation.

  • Preferred experience with MITRE ATT&CK, Atomic Red Team, adversary emulation, detection testing, BAS tools, or offensive security labs.

Leadership & Mentorship

  • Serve as a senior technical lead during significant cyber security investigations and incident response efforts.

  • Mentor SOC Leads, Security Analysts, Incident Responders, and Security Engineers on investigative and forensic methodologies.

  • Contribute to playbooks, runbooks, investigation standards, threat hunting procedures, and operational documentation.

  • Help mature the organization’s DFIR, Incident Response, Detection Engineering, Threat Hunting, and Security Automation capabilities.

  • Communicate effectively with technical teams, leadership, Legal, HR, Compliance, and business stakeholders.

What We Are Looking For:

  • 5–10+ years of experience in Cyber Security, Incident Response, DFIR, Threat Hunting, Detection Engineering, Security Operations, or related disciplines.

  • Proven experience leading enterprise-level cyber incident response investigations.

  • Hands-on experience with digital forensic analysis, evidence collection, malware analysis, and investigative reporting.

  • Experience working across cloud, hybrid, identity, endpoint, network, and on-premises enterprise environments.

  • Experience developing detections, automations, playbooks, scripts, queries, or engineering solutions that improve security outcomes.

Technical Skills

Strong understanding of:

  • Microsoft Entra ID, Active Directory, Azure, Microsoft 365, identity security, and enterprise authentication concepts.

  • Windows operating systems, endpoint telemetry, authentication logs, forensic artifacts, and persistence mechanisms.

  • Cloud security concepts across Azure, AWS, GCP, SaaS, identity, logging, and monitoring environments.

  • Incident response frameworks, cyber kill chain, MITRE ATT&CK, threat intelligence, and threat-informed defense.

  • Enterprise security operations including SIEM, EDR, NDR, SOAR, vulnerability data, network security, and email security.

Hands-On Experience With

  • SIEM platforms such as Microsoft Sentinel, Splunk, QRadar, or equivalent technologies.

  • EDR and XDR platforms such as Microsoft Defender XDR, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, or equivalent solutions.

  • Digital forensic tools, forensic imaging, artifact collection, timeline analysis, endpoint investigation, and evidence handling.

  • Scripting, querying, and automation using PowerShell, Python, Kusto Query Language, SQL, APIs, or equivalent technologies.

  • Detection engineering, threat hunting, malware triage, alert tuning, dashboards, correlation rules, and response workflows.

DFIR Technical Capabilities

  • Experience performing artifact-based investigations across endpoint, identity, email, cloud, and network data sources.

  • Knowledge of Windows forensic artifacts, registry analysis, event logs, authentication patterns, persistence techniques, and attacker behaviors.

  • Ability to analyze attacker activity including phishing, credential theft, lateral movement, privilege escalation, command execution, and data access.

  • Experience producing forensic timelines, investigative findings, executive summaries, and remediation recommendations.

  • Ability to operate independently during urgent or high-impact incidents while maintaining accuracy, documentation, and evidence integrity.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Cyber Security, Computer Science, Information Technology, Digital Forensics, or related field; equivalent experience considered.

  • Experience supporting legal, compliance, HR, fraud, insider risk, or regulatory investigations.

  • Experience conducting malware analysis, threat hunting, detection engineering, red teaming, penetration testing, or purple team exercises.

  • Experience experimenting with AI-assisted security tools, copilots, automation workflows, security agents, scripting, or personal lab environments.

  • Experience in Microsoft-focused enterprise environments, including Microsoft Sentinel, Defender XDR, Entra ID, Azure, Microsoft 365, and KQL.

Job Description

The University of Nevada, Las Vegas invites applications for Research Administrator, Pre Award with the Office of Sponsored Programs (REMOTE) [R0153457]

ROLE of the POSITION

The Research Administrator, Pre Award assists faculty members, principal investigators, and department grant administrators in the development, preparation, and submission of sponsored proposals for research, service projects, and other creative activities. The following are a few responsibilities but not limited to: Prepare, review and submit proposals and ensure proposals are complete, in compliance with university and NSHE/UNLV policies, state and federal laws and regulations, and align with the policies, procedures and requirements of sponsoring agencies. Assist faculty and staff with the development and review of proposal budgets. Submit applications through federal and non-federal online submission platforms to funding agencies including but not limited to NASA, NIH, NSF, DOE, etc. Submit highly complex proposals to an extensive variety of agencies involving one or more of the following situations: multiple departments/units; multiple institutions (subawards); institutional cost-sharing; institutional commitment proposals; training grant applications, etc. Educate and train faculty and staff on all aspects of proposal development and submission. Utilize and become proficient in Cayuse for grant management activities.

Primary Job Duties

Proposal Development & Submission: Provide critical analysis and guidance in the review and interpretation of funding opportunity announcements. Answer inquiries involving an explanation of rules, regulations, and procedures that require knowledge of the individual program and a high degree of problem-solving, and analytical and creative thinking. Responsible for managing a significant volume of proposals. Prepare, review, and educate faculty and staff on detailed proposal budgets. Provide proposal component review on budgets, required templates, standard forms, etc. Provide guidance to faculty and staff regarding research administration issues, interpreting PP&Gs and regulations, etc. Educate and Provide Training to Faculty and Staff: Assist in educating faculty, departmental administrators and other staff members in understanding all areas of proposal development and submission including proposal and budget development, and unique sponsor requirements. Educate and train faculty and staff on the use of the Cayuse grants management system. Special Projects and Assignments: Work independently or with others on various projects such as surveys, policy/procedure development, form development, or special reports. Participate in and contribute to process improvements. Maintain Knowledge of Federal Regulations and Sponsor Requirements: Maintain expertise in federal, state and university regulations, policies, and procedures. Regularly review federal sponsor policies and proposal guides and participate in webinars, trainings, and/or conferences to remain current on ever changing regulatory compliance pertaining to grants and research administration.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Knowledge of the functional areas of sponsored program administration (Pre-award through Post-award) and a good general knowledge of the nature of research in all academic disciplines.

General understanding of the nature and requirements of sponsored project contracts, grants, cooperative agreements, requests for proposal or quote.

Understanding of research administration guidelines of Federal and non-Federal sponsors supporting research and educational activities.

Possess knowledge of federal procurement regulations, including the CFR & FAR, agency CFR/FAR implementations, and the Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200 and audit regulations (Single Audit) that pertain to institutions of higher education.

Knowledgeable of sponsor-specific policies, intellectual property policy, conflict of interest requirements, publication rights, application of indirect cost rates and other complex concepts in research administration

Experience working in grant submission platforms such as ASSIST, Research.gov, Grants.gov, NSPIRES, etc. Experience with Excel and budget development.

Demonstrated customer service focus and an ability to communicate verbally and in writing clearly and effectively, presenting ideas, answering questions and documenting activities.

Strong analytical, organizational and interpersonal skills.

Self-starter, diplomatic, pro-active, ability to manage stress. Ability to handle multiple projects and deadlines simultaneously.

Ability and capacity to work with a high degree of independence within a fast paced environment that is deadline driven and a multi-tasking operating environment.

Ability to interact and collaborate with multiple constituencies as well as excellent analytical, organizational, interpersonal, oral, and written communication skills.

Demonstrated ability to interpret policies and act independently in a highly complex regulatory/legal environment.

Central office operations related to working in a Pre Award office; to include proposal submission, review and interpretation of funding agencies/sponsors.

  • Du bist im Buchinhalt die Ansprechpartnerin für unsere Creator und übersetzt deren Wünsche in eine Geschichte, die funktioniert.
  • Du hältst den Erscheinungstermin, planst rückwärts von der Druckfreigabe und sagst früh Bescheid, wenn es eng wird.

Qualifikation

  • Mindestens zwei bis drei Jahre Erfahrung im Lektorat von Belletristik für Kinder oder Jugendliche, im Verlag, in einer Agentur, bei einem Buchpackager oder freiberuflich. Mehr ist ausdrücklich willkommen.
  • Gefühl für Storyaufbau, Figurenentwicklung, Perspektive und Dialog. Du erkennst, warum ein Kapitel nicht zieht, und kannst es benennen.
  • Du liest Kinder- und Jugendromane auch privat. Wer nur Sachbücher liest, hat für diese Stelle das falsche Ohr.
  • Sicheres Korrektorat, Erfahrung mit Reihen und mit festen Erscheinungsterminen.
  • Deutsch auf muttersprachlichem Niveau.
  • Du arbeitest im Home-Office selbstorganisiert, hältst Zusagen ein und meldest Probleme, bevor sie Termine kosten.
  • Sicher im Word-Änderungsmodus. Teams und ClickUp lernst du bei uns in einer Woche.

Kein Ausschluss: Sachbuch, Schulbuch oder Wissenschaft im Lebenslauf sind in Ordnung, solange du Belletristik für Kinder belegen kannst. Erfahrung mit YouTubern oder Influencern brauchst du nicht, die bringen wir dir bei. Storygefühl bringst du mit.

Wer liefert, verdient hier mehr, und zwar automatisch, nicht nach Verhandlung.

jobs.excerpt: Controller, Accounting Operations & FP&AJoin a remote-first, sponsor-backed professional services business at a stage where the finance function is becoming a true growth lever.
jobs.description:
Controller, Accounting Operations & FP&A

Join a remote-first, sponsor-backed professional services business at a stage where the finance function is becoming a true growth lever. This is an internal Controller role for someone who is already strong in accounting operations and wants a broader seat across faster close, cleaner reporting, FP&A support, acquisition integration, automation, and direct partnership with senior finance and executive leadership.

The Opportunity

The company is scaling through a mix of core services growth, new offerings, and acquisition activity. The finance team needs a hands-on Controller who can keep the accounting engine accurate and dependable while helping modernize how the business closes, reports, forecasts, and integrates new lines of business.

This is not a narrow bookkeeping seat, and it is not a hands-off VP Finance role. It is ideal for a highly capable Controller who wants to stay close to the GL, own the accounting operating cadence, and build toward broader FP&A and strategic finance exposure over time.

What You Will Own

Accounting Operations

Own day-to-day accounting operations across payroll, accounts receivable, accounts payable, reconciliations, month-end close, and reporting workflows.

Lead the close process with a focus on speed, accuracy, reviewability, and repeatability.

Maintain clean financial records that support leadership reporting, board reporting, audit readiness, and future lender-related data requests.

Oversee and develop one direct report in a senior accountant / accounting specialist capacity.

Support required registrations, compliance-related finance administration, and other operational finance needs as they arise.

Reporting, FP&A, and Leadership Support

Build and improve financial reporting packages so leadership can review results earlier, identify insights faster, and make better decisions.

Support monthly variance analysis, fluctuation analysis, forecasting, budgeting, and longer-term planning exercises.

Help prepare operational finance inputs for board reporting, annual budgeting, sponsor-backed reporting, audit readiness, and valuation-related needs.

Partner with the finance leader on lender-facing data preparation if and when the company moves into lender relationships.

Translate accurate accounting outputs into useful finance insights for a scaling professional services business.

Systems, Automation, and Process Modernization

Assess the current finance and accounting tech stack and help determine what should be automated, upgraded, or replaced over time.

Improve capacity in the controller function through better processes and tools rather than simply adding headcount.

Identify opportunities to automate month-end close, reconciliations, AP workflows, reporting packages, and recurring data pulls.

Support future ERP, accounting system, forecasting tool, or related finance systems implementation work.

Acquisition Integration

Help integrate accounting operations for a recently acquired business line currently relying on informal or part-time bookkeeping support.

Create a more scalable accounting process for the acquired business, including fixed-price services revenue and related reporting.

Support acquisition-related accounting integration work such as GL alignment, reporting consistency, data cleanup, and operating cadence.

Bring practical judgment to a business where acquisition activity and integration work are expected to remain part of the finance environment.

What Makes You a Strong Fit

You have strong Controller-level experience owning accounting operations in a smaller or mid-sized business where finance and accounting responsibilities are not overly siloed.

You are comfortable being accountable for the GL, close, reporting accuracy, and accounting process discipline.

You have meaningful exposure to FP&A, forecasting, variance analysis, budgeting, or board reporting, even if your core strength is still accounting.

You have worked in a sponsor-backed, PE-backed, VC-backed, or similarly high-accountability environment where speed, reporting quality, and leadership visibility matter.

You have experience with professional services, project-based accounting, fixed-price services revenue, or other operationally complex revenue models.

You can support a business with a mix of services and subscription-style revenue, even if project-based accounting has been the more complex part of your background.

You have either participated in acquisition integration work before or have strong adjacent experience organizing new entities, business lines, systems, and reporting flows.

You are comfortable working directly with senior finance leadership and being a reliable leverage point for better reporting, analysis, and operating cadence.

You are hands-on, fast, precise, and willing to improve the process while still doing the underlying accounting work well.

Nice-to-Haves

ERP implementation, accounting system implementation, forecasting tool implementation, or finance systems modernization experience.

Automation experience across close, reconciliations, AP, reporting, or recurring finance workflows.

Experience preparing data for lenders, debt reporting, covenant tracking, or quarterly lender packages.

Familiarity with government contracting, federal contractor environments, regulated services businesses, or compliance-heavy operating models.

Experience in a multi-service-line business with project-based, fixed-price, managed services, and subscription-style revenue.

Audit support experience in a sponsor-backed or acquisition-oriented environment.

The First 90 Days

First 30 Days

Learn the current accounting operations, reporting cadence, systems, team structure, and business model.

Identify the biggest opportunities to streamline month-end close and reporting package preparation.

Begin improving reporting workflows so leadership can review results earlier and with more confidence.

First 60 Days

Take meaningful ownership of integrating accounting operations for the recently acquired business line.

Move acquired-business accounting away from informal or part-time support toward a scalable internal process.

Continue tightening the monthly close and recurring reporting cadence.

First 90 Days

Establish a clearer operating rhythm across close, reporting, finance inputs, and leadership review.

Help prepare for upcoming budgeting, audit, valuation, and sponsor-backed reporting needs.

Funnel Leasing Inc., is hiring for a Event and Conference Manager that can 'work from anywhere' in the U.S. The Event and Conference Manager owns Funnel’s events and conferences calendar end to end: ideation, logistics, vendor negotiation, branding, and on-site execution. This role also owns the commercial engine behind every event: partnering with SDRs and sales on targeted outreach before events, working with demand gen to make sure every lead gets the right follow-up after, and supporting ABM campaigns that turn event presence into pipeline.

Industry events in-market events and Funnel’s user conference, The Forum, drive significant portion of annual pipeline. This is a revenue-critical role, not just a logistics one. The salary range for this role is $80,000 - $95,000 per year.

Major projects this person will own and be accountable for:

  • 4 annual industry conferences with tradeshow/booth and VIP party presence
  • 1 annual user conference (The Forum)
  • 1 annual employee conference (Funnel Fest)
  • Support for up to a dozen local apartment associations, working with account reps
  • 6 in-office events (board meetings, leadership offsites, VIP meetings)
  • Regional Lunch & Learn events
  • Regional VIP events
  • LinkedIn Live events and webinars

Why Funnel?

We are a 'work from anywhere' in the U.S. SaaS company that centers our services on the renter experience. We develop amazing software that has revolutionized the #proptech industry. And did we mention we have an amazing team that is on #FunnelFire!? Oh, did we forget to tell you we have unlimited PTO, benefits that begin on your first day of employment, P.I.N.K. core values that ROCK, and our team puts the FUN in Funnel!

Who is Funnel Leasing?

Have you ever rented an apartment and wished the process could be better? At Funnel we do too. We know we need to make the process of renting an apartment as easy as purchasing socks on Amazon. We’ve created cloud-based marketing and leasing software that delivers the ultimate rental experience for everyone involved in the process. We’re in the process of transforming the real estate industry through cutting-edge technology built, sold, and supported by the most passionate people you’ll meet.

The Event and Conference Manager essential roles and responsibilities include, but are not limited to the following:

Roles and responsibilities

Event Strategy & Execution

  • Conceptualize differentiated booth designs and VIP experiences with external vendors
  • Build and maintain the events calendar with the marketing team
  • Work with graphic design to finalize promotional assets, swag and VIP gifts
  • Own all event logistics: venue, A/V, catering, shipping, and vendor negotiation for the best rates and terms

  • Manage registration sites and event landing pages

Pipeline & Sales Partnership

  • Own outreach planning with SDRs and sales for every event: target account lists, invite cadence, and follow-up ownership before attendees ever arrive
  • Partner with demand gen on post-event follow-up so every lead gets the right next step, fast
  • Support ABM campaigns tied to (and independent of) events: account selection, personalized outreach, and executive experiences for top targets
  • Work with sales to confirm the right people are being invited and shown up for, not just headcount
  • Share attendee lists, overview decks, and other pertinent event information with internal stakeholders
  • Track and report event and campaign ROI: pipeline sourced and influenced, cost per lead, follow-up conversion, to continuously improve strategy
  • Stay current on industry trends, market dynamics, and buyer behavior to keep event strategy sharp
  • Develop relationships with other partners in our space to encourage collaborative events

Team & Office

  • Recruit, train, and manage on-site event staff and any contracted support
  • Lead the Funnel event team on-site to build attendee relationships that support sales objectives
  • (For local Tampa candidates) Keep the Odessa, FL office presentable and stocked; staff it up to 2 days/week to coordinate deliveries and prep for on-site meetings

Budget & Vendor Management

  • Develop and manage event budgets and marketing plans against approved objectives
  • Evaluate new event opportunities before committing budget or staff time
  • Administer all phases of the event function: planning, marketing, servicing, and admin, within approved budget

Culture

  • Creative. You think of outside-the-box ideas that have a lasting impact on prospects and event attendees.
  • Style. You’re often told you have great taste and stay on top of trends and culture.
  • Hyper-organized. You manage (and can cite) highly interdependent, complex projects and keep every workstream on track without losing details along the way.
  • Sales-minded. You obsess over the persona each event is meant to reach, and make sure sales, SDRs, and demand gen are amplifying your efforts toward the right attendees.
  • A team player. You collaborate daily with Marketing, Sales, SDRs, Demand Gen, Product, and other teams, and can work across a range of disciplines to get things done.
  • Trendsetter. You push the status quo and look for a better way to improve Funnel’s buyer journey. You keep up to date with others pushing boundaries.
  • Performs other duties as assigned and modified at the manager’s discretion.

Education, Work Experience, and Certifications

  • Hotel/hospitality degree a plus, not required
  • 6+ years of progressive event or field marketing management experience; B2B SaaS or similar preferred
  • Hands-on experience setting up and administering event management platforms (e.g. Whova, Cvent, Splash, Bizzabo, or similar) and other registration/lead capture tools
  • Familiarity with CRM and marketing automation platforms (e.g. Salesforce, HubSpot, Marketo, or similar) for outreach and follow-up tracking
  • Exposure to ABM strategy and execution a plus
  • Excellent interpersonal skills and a track record working cross-functionally, especially with sales and SDR teams
  • Excellent presentation skills, both virtual and in-person
  • Proven track record of running events that produce pipeline, not just attendance
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills
  • Local candidates to Odessa/Tampa, FL a plus

About the opportunity

CloudFactory is looking for participants to support a short-term transaction validation project that we are administering on behalf of a global payments processing company.

The project is designed to help evaluate the accuracy of how payment transactions are matched to individuals.

As a participant, you'll review a set of recent payment transactions and indicate whether or not you recognize each transaction as one you made yourself.

How it works

If selected for the project:

  1. You'll provide the email address(es) you use with selected merchants, subscriptions, apps, or online accounts.
  2. Our payments processing client will use those email address(es) to identify payment transactions it believes are associated with you and securely provide a list of those transactions for the project.

The information shown may include details such as the merchant name, date, amount, payment method, card identifier, and card issuer to help you recognize each transaction.
  4. You'll indicate whether or not you recognize each transaction as one you made yourself and, where helpful, add a short note.

The activity is expected to take approximately 1–2 hours.

You will not be asked to provide or upload your own transaction history, bank statements, full card number, online banking login credentials, banking password, PIN, or CVV.

Please note that this is a data validation activity only.

Requirements

  • Be 18 years of age or older.
  • Currently reside in United States.
  • Be an active debit and/or credit card user.
  • Have made purchases or payments within the last three months across a variety of merchants and services included in our eligibility questionnaire.
  • Be able to recognize your own recent purchases and transactions.
  • Have access to the email address(es) you use with the merchants and services included in our eligibility questionnaire.
  • Be comfortable providing those email address(es) if selected for the project.
  • Be willing to review approximately 50 transactions and confirm whether or not you recognize them as your own.

Privacy and consent

Because this project involves personal and financial transaction information, privacy and informed consent are essential.

Before participating, you'll receive our Participant Consent & Confidentiality Terms, which explain how your personal information and transaction data will be used and processed as part of the project.

Job Description

Certificates and Licenses: Valid Special Education Texas Teaching Certificate or comparable state educator certification.

Residency: Texas

Salary: Around $60,000

SUMMARY: The Special Education Local & State Testing Coordinator is responsible for overseeing and coordinating all special education-related local and state assessment processes to ensure compliance with federal, state, district, and testing program requirements. This position serves as the primary point of contact for special education testing accommodations, assessment participation decisions, testing escalations, and specialized testing supports. The position collaborates closely with Special Education Compliance staff, campus administrators, counselors, data teams, testing personnel, and families to ensure students with disabilities receive appropriate testing accommodations and equitable access to assessments while maintaining testing integrity and compliance.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS: Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential duties.

Special Education Assessment Coordination

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for all special education state and district-wide testing accommodations.
  • Manage and monitor testing accommodations for district assessments, TELPAS, STAAR, EOCs, and other state-required assessments.
  • Address and resolve escalations related to testing accommodations from parents, administrators, teachers, and testing personnel.
  • Respond to parent concerns and inquiries regarding state testing participation, accommodations, and testing procedures.
  • Support the Special Education Compliance Team with complex ARD committee decisions and unique accommodation needs.
  • Provide ongoing support to Academic Testing Coordinators, Campus Operations staff, and campus administrators throughout all testing windows.
  • Manage and coordinate at-home testing requests and documentation.
  • Submit and track testing irregularities involving accommodations during active testing windows.
  • Review and monitor testing participation decisions to ensure appropriate implementation and compliance.

Accommodation Management and Compliance

  • Monitor initial ARDs to ensure timely communication and implementation of testing accommodations.
  • Monitor pending Transfer Student Agreements (TSAs) and students with pending records to ensure accommodations are implemented without delay.
  • Review all supplemental aids and accommodations for compliance with Texas Education Agency (TEA) guidelines.
  • Review pending TEA-approved accommodation requests and collect required supporting documentation.
  • Coordinate submission of ARFs to the State Testing Manager.
  • Communicate TEA accommodation decisions to IEP teams and families.
  • Ensure all accommodations are appropriately reflected in Frontline, TestHound, and related testing systems.
  • Verify accommodations are documented for all applicable assessments and subject areas.

Audit, Monitoring, and Quality Assurance

  • Conduct routine audits of special education testing data and records.
  • Verify accurate entry of state testing information into Frontline.
  • Ensure all active special education students are accounted for within applicable reporting systems.
  • Review accommodation documentation for compliance with state testing requirements.
  • Maintain records of discrepancies, compliance concerns, and accommodation errors identified during audits.
  • Collaborate with the Special Education Compliance Team to ensure required IEP amendments are completed promptly.
  • Monitor and follow up on identified IEP amendments related to testing participation and accommodations.
  • Verify Participation Sufficient decisions are supported by appropriate ARD documentation.

Specialized Testing Support Coordination

  • Maintain tracking systems for students requiring printed testing materials.
  • Coordinate submission of printed material requests to the State Testing Manager by designated deadlines.
  • Maintain tracking systems for students requiring unique accommodations, including:
    • Service animals
    • Spanish STAAR assessments
    • Assistive technology devices
    • TEA-approved accommodations
    • Significant health supports
    • Nursing assistance
    • Other individualized accommodations
  • Communicate student-specific testing needs to assigned testing sites prior to testing windows.
  • Maintain tracking systems for students requiring CPI-trained support staff during testing.
    • Coordinate testing schedules to ensure appropriate staff coverage and support.
    • Communicate finalized testing schedules to all relevant testing sites.

Documentation and Resource Management

  • Upload and maintain testing-related resources and documentation in designated Microsoft Lists and district systems.
  • Ensure required testing resources are available and organized, including:
    • Supplemental aids
    • Multiplication charts
    • Graphic organizers
    • Behavior Intervention Plans (BIPs)
    • Health Accommodation Action Plans
  • Maintain accurate documentation and records related to accommodation implementation and testing support services.
  • Track and monitor accepted EOC performance decisions from previous and current ARD committees.

Collaboration & Compliance

  • Ensure all assessment processes comply with TEA guidelines, district procedures, and special education regulations.
  • Partner with the Special Education Compliance Team to address complex testing situations and compliance concerns.
  • Collaborate with the State Testing Manager regarding accommodation requests, testing irregularities, and procedural guidance.
  • Support the implementation of compliance corrective actions as needed.
  • Maintain confidentiality and security of all student assessment information and testing materials.
  • Ensure testing practices align with state test security requirements and ethical standards.

Stakeholder Communication, Training & Resource Development

  • Serve as the primary liaison between families, school personnel, and testing teams regarding special education testing matters.
  • Provide guidance and support to parents concerning testing accommodations and participation decisions.
  • Facilitate communication between IEP teams, counselors, testing coordinators, and campus administrators.
  • Develop and maintain testing resources, guidance documents, and procedural materials.
  • Provide training and technical assistance regarding accommodations, testing procedures, and compliance expectations.
  • Communicate testing schedules, accommodation requirements, and updates to relevant stakeholders.

Data & Monitoring

  • Generate and maintain accommodation reports using Frontline and other district data systems.
  • Develop and maintain accommodation tracking spreadsheets and monitoring tools.
  • Utilize reporting systems to identify discrepancies and monitor implementation of accommodations.
  • Monitor TELPAS Change Request Rosters and accommodation uploads throughout testing windows.
  • Generate accommodation reports for the Data Team to support TestHound uploads.
  • Monitor Participation Sufficient decisions and update EOC rosters throughout testing cycles.
  • Track newly identified Special Education and Emergent Bilingual students for accommodation implementation.
  • Analyze testing data and compliance trends to identify areas for improvement.

Collaboration Across Teams

  • Collaborate with Special Education Compliance staff to ensure accurate documentation and compliance.
  • Partner with lead counselors to monitor graduation requirements and EOC completion for seniors.
  • Support campus administrators and testing coordinators during all assessment windows.
  • Work closely with the Data Team to ensure accurate accommodation uploads and testing system updates.
  • Collaborate with nurses, related service providers, assistive technology specialists, and CPI-trained staff to facilitate student testing needs.
  • Coordinate with ARD committees and educational teams regarding participation decisions and accommodation implementation.
  • Serve as a resource for district and school personnel regarding special education assessment requirements.

Supervisory Responsibilities: This position has no formal supervisory responsibilities.

MINIMUM REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Education, Special Education, Educational Leadership, Counseling or related field
  • Three (3) years of experience in Special Education services, compliance, assessment coordination, or related educational roles.
  • Experience participating in ARD/IEP processes and accommodation planning.
  • Federal and state special education laws and regulations.
  • Texas Education Agency (TEA) assessment policies and accommodation guidelines.
  • ARD/IEP processes and documentation requirements.
  • State and local assessment administration procedures.
  • Test security and confidentiality requirements.
  • Special education compliance and monitoring procedures.
  • Assistive technology and accommodation supports for students with disabilities.
  • Exceptional organizational and project management skills.
  • Data analysis and reporting skills.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Documentation review and audit skills.
  • Training and presentation skills.
  • Manage multiple priorities and deadlines during high-volume testing periods.
  • Interpret and apply complex testing regulations and compliance requirements.
  • Collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams and stakeholders.
  • Maintain accuracy and attention to detail in data management and monitoring activities.
  • Provide leadership and guidance in complex accommodation and assessment situations.
  • Microsoft 365 (Outlook, Word, Excel) proficiency.
  • Ability to travel 25% of the time
  • Ability to clear required background check

DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Experience with state assessment administration and testing compliance preferred.
  • Experience utilizing educational data systems, student information systems, and accommodation tracking tools.
  • Experience providing staff training and technical assistance.
  • Counseling certification.
  • CPI certification or familiarity with Crisis Prevention Intervention practices.

WORK ENVIRONMENT: The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • This position is virtual with residents of Texas strongly preferred. Residents of states contiguous to Texas may also be considered.

Summary

The Clinics Nurse Practitioner/Physician Assistant is responsible for the primary care of those individuals directed to the clinics via hospital based programs.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Demonstrates clinical competence to provide adult or family primary care through telehealth modalities, with or without sub-specialty expertise, within the APP's scope of practice, clinical privileges, and applicable laws and regulations.
  • Provides primary care medical services for assigned patients through telehealth, including preventive care, evaluation and treatment of acute illnesses and injuries when clinically appropriate for virtual management, chronic disease management, health maintenance, and referrals to appropriate in-person services, specialties, or facilities.
  • Conducts comprehensive and focused patient assessments through video and other approved telehealth modalities, including obtaining an appropriate medical history and performing an appropriate virtual examination.
  • Recognizes the clinical limitations of telehealth and appropriately determines when an in-person physical examination, diagnostic testing, laboratory services, imaging, urgent care, emergency care, or other in-person evaluation is necessary to safely assess and manage the patient.
  • Verifies patient identity and location and follows applicable telehealth consent, privacy, security, documentation, and regulatory requirements.
  • Orders, performs, and interprets diagnostic tests as appropriate, recognizing when testing or diagnostic evaluation requires coordination with an in-person healthcare location.
  • Prescribes medications, therapy, and other specialized medical care consistent with the standard of care, scope of practice, clinical privileges, organizational policies, and applicable laws and regulations.
  • Performs appropriate medical procedures within scope of practice as defined by licensing requirements and the health system's credentialing and privileging processes and appropriately identifies procedures or interventions that cannot be safely performed through telehealth.
  • Considers a thorough range of treatment and preventive options and arrives at a recommended course of action that is age appropriate, culturally appropriate, realistic, attainable, and appropriate to the patient's ability to access necessary in-person services.
  • Appropriately manages patient care and health status following initiation of a treatment or preventive plan through virtual follow-up, monitoring, and reassessment, and adjusts the plan of care as warranted.
  • Communicates effectively with patients and families in a virtual environment so that they understand their diagnosis, treatment plan, medications, follow-up requirements, and circumstances that require escalation to in-person or emergency care.
  • Educates and encourages patients to become active participants in their healthcare and provides appropriate patient education materials, digital resources, and self-management tools.
  • Documents telehealth encounters accurately and in a timely manner within the electronic medical record to facilitate continuity, coordination, and quality of care. Demonstrates the ability to distinguish between normal and abnormal findings based on available patient history, virtual examination, diagnostic information, and other clinical data, and recognizes when the limitations of virtual assessment require additional in-person evaluation.
  • Makes appropriate referrals to physicians, specialists, community agencies, and in-person healthcare services based on the patient's clinical needs.
  • Collaborates with and consults supervising physician(s) and other members of the healthcare team when appropriate and required by policy. Completes chart review as required by health system policies and escalates care appropriately when a patient's condition exceeds the APP's training, expertise, scope of practice, or the capabilities of telehealth.
  • Coordinates patient care across primary care clinics, specialty services, laboratory, imaging, emergency services, urgent care, and other healthcare resources to ensure appropriate follow-up and continuity of care.
  • Assists with EHR inbox coverage and patient triage, including evaluation of telephone calls, electronic messages, test results, medication requests, and other patient communications within scope of practice.
  • Provides additional virtual clinical support for patients whose primary provider is out of the office, including appropriate assessment, treatment, follow-up, and coordination of care.
  • Provides same-day and urgent telehealth visits when clinically appropriate and directs patients to appropriate in-person urgent care or emergency services when the patient's condition cannot be safely managed virtually.
  • Responds to telephone calls, electronic messages, and other patient communications in a timely manner and determines when a communication requires conversion to a telehealth visit or in person evaluation.
  • Utilizes telehealth technology, the electronic medical record, and other approved digital health tools effectively to provide safe, efficient, and patient-centered care. Troubleshoots routine technology issues and appropriately transitions the encounter to another modality or in-person care when technology limitations affect safe patient care.
  • Maintains a professional, patient-centered virtual environment and establishes effective therapeutic relationships with patients through video and other approved telehealth modalities.
  • Adheres to all relevant policies, procedures, practice guidelines, telehealth requirements, professional standards, and applicable federal and state laws and regulations.
  • Supports appropriate billing for professional services through timely, accurate documentation and maintains adequate knowledge of the health system's telehealth, coding, billing, and documentation requirements.
  • Reviews and follows up on complaints, concerns, and patient feedback related to medical care and the telehealth experience.
  • Regularly attends and actively participates in clinic staff meetings, physician/NP/PA meetings, Primary Care Committee meetings, and other meetings as requested.
  • Participates in community education and other professional activities to promote access to care, practice growth, health education, and community wellness as requested.
  • Maintains positive, caring, and supportive relationships with patients, families, care team members, and clinic staff while working effectively within a virtual care environment.
  • Demonstrates System Values in performance and behavior.
  • Complies with System policies and procedures.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Supervisory Responsibilities

No supervisory responsibilities.

Education and Experience

Nurse Practitioner
Bachelor’s degree (B.S.) from four-year college or university; Graduation from a National League of Nursing (NLN), Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (CCNE) or equivalent accredited school of nursing. The nurse shall have completed a nursing education program that included clinical experiences with actual patients under the supervision of qualified faculty. Must be certified by the American Academy of Nurse Practitioners (AANP) or the American Nurses credentialing Center (ANCC).
Physician Assistant
Completion of a Physician Assistant program accredited by the Accreditation Review Commission on Education for the Physician Assistant.
Telehealth Competencies
Demonstrates proficiency in providing patient-centered care through telehealth modalities; effectively utilizes telehealth technology and electronic health record systems; demonstrates sound clinical judgment regarding the limitations of virtual assessment; appropriately identifies patients requiring in-person or emergency evaluation; and effectively coordinates care across multiple healthcare locations and services.
Licenses, Certifications
Required if working in departments 17092-MSC Urgent Care Truckee, 17093-MSC Urgent Care Tahoe City or 17094-MSC Urgent Care Squaw Valley and hired after 8/24/2020: Employee will be enrolled in the Resuscitation Quality Improvement (RQI) Advanced Cardiovascular Life Support (ACLS) Entry or Prep Curriculum (depending on their previous ACLS certification) which must be completed within three (3) months of hire. Anyone hired prior to 8/24/2020 will have three (3) months to obtain ACLS certificate.

Nurse Practitioner:

  • Current ANCC (American Nurses Credentialing Center) or AANP (American Academy of Nurse Practitioners) certification required. Current PNCB (Pediatric Nursing Certification Board) or current ANCC is required if requesting to work in pediatrics.
  • Current BLS (Basic Life Support) and must maintain certification at all times.
  • Must have a Collaborative Service Agreement (CA) or evidence of Supervising Physician Agreement (NV State Medical Board), as applicable, with a designated supervising physician member of the Hospital’s medical staff (upon hiring, manager will initiate).
  • Current, unrestricted DEA certificate in CA and/or NV, as applicable (Schedules II-V). Nevada Pharmacy Board certificate, if applying to work in NV.
  • Ability to participate in a federally funded program (Medicare and Medicaid)

  • Current, unrestricted DEA certificate in CA and/or NV, as applicable (Schedules II-V). Nevada Pharmacy Board certificate, if applying to work in NV
  • Ability to participate in a federally funded program (Medicare and Medicaid)

jobs.description:
UX/UI Designer – Figma, Product Design & User Experience | Remote

Position Type: Full-Time, Remote
Working Hours: U.S. Client Business Hours

About the Role

At Pavago, one of our clients is hiring a UX/UI Designer to create intuitive, visually polished, and high-performing digital experiences across web and mobile products.

This is more than a visual design role. You’ll own the design process from user research and UX strategy through wireframing, prototyping, high-fidelity UI design, design systems, and developer handoff.

You’ll work closely with Product Managers, Engineers, QA, and leadership to understand user problems and translate them into digital experiences that are easy to use, scalable, accessible, and aligned with business objectives.

If you combine strong UX thinking with polished UI execution and enjoy solving real product problems through design, this role is a strong fit.

What You’ll Own

User Research & UX Strategy

  • Conduct user interviews, surveys, usability testing, and behavioral analysis
  • Identify user needs, pain points, and friction across digital experiences
  • Translate research into:
    • Personas
    • User journeys
    • User flows
    • Information architecture
    • Wireframes
  • Use behavioral and analytics tools such as:
    • Hotjar
    • FullStory
    • Google Analytics
  • Combine qualitative and quantitative insights to identify UX opportunities
  • Recommend improvements based on user behavior, research, and product goals

Wireframing & Prototyping

  • Create low-fidelity wireframes to validate concepts and workflows
  • Build interactive prototypes for usability testing and stakeholder review
  • Develop high-fidelity product mockups using:
    • Figma
    • Adobe XD
    • Sketch
  • Rapidly iterate based on:
    • User testing
    • Stakeholder feedback
    • QA findings
  • Clearly communicate interaction patterns and intended product behavior
  • Move concepts efficiently from early exploration to production-ready design

UI & Product Design

  • Design clean, modern, and user-friendly interfaces
  • Create responsive experiences across:
    • Desktop
    • Tablet
    • Mobile
  • Balance usability, aesthetics, accessibility, and business objectives
  • Design user flows and conversion paths that minimize friction
  • Apply strong visual hierarchy, typography, spacing, and layout principles
  • Ensure interfaces are visually polished and production-ready
  • Maintain consistency across features and product experiences

Design Systems & Scalability

  • Build and maintain scalable design systems and component libraries
  • Establish consistent standards for:
    • Typography
    • Color
    • Spacing
    • Layouts
    • Components
    • Interaction patterns
  • Create reusable components that improve design and development efficiency
  • Maintain organized design files, assets, specifications, and documentation
  • Ensure consistency across products, features, and platforms
  • Evolve design systems as product requirements grow

Accessibility & Usability

  • Apply WCAG accessibility standards throughout the design process
  • Consider:
    • Contrast
    • Readability
    • Keyboard accessibility
    • Responsiveness
    • Overall usability
  • Conduct usability reviews
  • Identify opportunities to simplify complex workflows
  • Improve:
    • Task completion
    • Navigation
    • Conversion paths
    • Overall product usability
  • Incorporate accessibility into designs from the beginning rather than treating it as a final check

Product & Engineering Collaboration

  • Work closely with:
    • Product Managers
    • Developers
    • QA
    • Leadership
  • Participate in sprint planning, product discussions, and feature prioritization
  • Collaborate with engineering throughout implementation rather than only at handoff
  • Deliver developer-ready designs using:
    • Figma Dev Mode
    • Zeplin
    • InVision Inspect
  • Provide clear specifications, assets, and interaction documentation
  • Review implemented designs
  • Identify and resolve inconsistencies before release
  • Help ensure the final product accurately reflects the intended user experience

Requirements

  • 2+ years of professional UX/UI or Product Design experience
  • Strong portfolio demonstrating:
    • UX problem-solving
    • UI craftsmanship
    • Responsive design
    • Product design thinking
  • Advanced proficiency with:
    • Figma
    • Adobe XD
    • Sketch
  • Experience creating:
    • User flows
    • Wireframes
    • Interactive prototypes
    • High-fidelity interfaces
    • Responsive layouts
    • Design systems
  • Strong understanding of:
    • UX and usability principles
    • Interaction design
    • Accessibility
    • Responsive design
    • Mobile-first design
  • Strong written and verbal English communication skills
  • Ability to clearly explain and defend design decisions
  • Ability to collaborate effectively in a remote product environment
  • Availability during U.S. client business hours

Preferred Experience

  • Experience designing:
    • SaaS products
    • Mobile applications
    • E-commerce platforms
  • Experience building or maintaining scalable design systems
  • Familiarity with:
    • HTML/CSS fundamentals
    • Developer workflows
    • Agile/Scrum environments
  • Experience with behavioral analytics tools such as:
    • Hotjar
    • FullStory
    • Google Analytics
  • Experience conducting A/B tests or design experiments
  • Understanding of Conversion Rate Optimization (CRO)
  • Experience collaborating directly with engineering teams through implementation

Tools & Technology

Figma | Figma Dev Mode | Adobe XD | Sketch | Zeplin | InVision Inspect | Hotjar | FullStory | Google Analytics | HTML/CSS | Design Systems | Prototyping & Usability Testing Tools

What Makes You a Strong Fit

You’ll likely thrive in this role if you:

  • Think about user journeys and product problems, not just individual screens
  • Combine strong visual design skills with practical UX thinking
  • Can clearly explain the reasoning behind your design decisions
  • Are comfortable using research and data to challenge assumptions
  • Understand how UX impacts adoption, engagement, conversion, and satisfaction
  • Collaborate effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders
  • Care about consistency, accessibility, and the small details that make products feel polished
  • Can iterate quickly without sacrificing design quality
  • Understand how designs translate into real products during development
  • Take ownership from initial research through final implementation

What a Typical Day Looks Like

Your day may begin by reviewing user behavior, product feedback, or upcoming feature requirements to identify UX opportunities and potential friction.

Throughout the day, you could create user flows and wireframes, build and test interactive prototypes, design polished interfaces in Figma, or refine the product’s design system.

You’ll collaborate closely with Product and Engineering during sprint execution, incorporate feedback from usability testing and QA, and prepare developer-ready designs with clear specifications and interaction details.

You’ll also review implemented features to ensure the final experience maintains the intended design quality and consistency.

In short: you turn user needs and business requirements into intuitive, scalable, accessible, and visually polished digital products.

Key Metrics for Success

  • Improved product usability and user satisfaction
  • Increased engagement and product adoption
  • Reduced friction across critical user journeys
  • Improved task completion and conversion flows
  • Consistent implementation of design systems
  • Reduced design-related development revisions
  • On-time delivery of developer-ready designs
  • Strong accessibility and responsive design standards
  • High-quality implementation of approved designs
  • Positive feedback from users and internal stakeholders

Why This Role Stands Out

  • End-to-end ownership of UX and UI design
  • Opportunity to influence real product strategy and user experience
  • Close collaboration with Product and Engineering leadership
  • Opportunity to build and improve scalable design systems
  • Use of research and analytics to influence product decisions
  • Hands-on involvement from discovery through implementation
  • Fully remote environment aligned with U.S. clients
  • Strong career progression into:
    • Senior Product Designer
    • Lead UX/UI Designer
    • Design Systems Lead
    • Head of Product Design

Interview Process

  1. Initial Application
  2. Spark Hire One-Way Video Interview
  3. Video Interview with Pavago Recruiter
  4. Portfolio Review + Practical Design Task
  5. Client Interview
  6. Offer & Background Verification

Spark Hire Video Interview – Required

As part of the application process, all candidates are required to complete a one-way video interview through Spark Hire.

After completing the first step of your application, you’ll receive a Spark Hire invitation by email with instructions to record and submit your video responses.

Completion of the Spark Hire video is required to be considered for the next stage. Please check your inbox as well as your spam or junk folder for the invitation.

Apply Now

If you have a strong UX/UI portfolio, are highly proficient in Figma, and can take a product from research and wireframes through polished, developer-ready UI, we’d love to hear from you.

Apply today and help create digital products that are intuitive, accessible, scalable, visually polished, and genuinely enjoyable to use.

LionHeart is a veteran-owned power generation company seeking a Senior Power Generation Technical Specialist to help solve our most difficult electrical and mechanical field problems.

Hybrid Cloud Architect - Remote

Bright Vision Technologies is a technology consulting and software development company delivering cloud, AI, data, and enterprise solutions across the United States.
This is a fantastic opportunity to join an established and well-respected organization offering tremendous career growth potential.

Job Title: Hybrid Cloud Architect
Location: 100% Remote (U.S.)
Position Type: Full-time, Direct W2
Salary Range: $100,000–$150,000 Annually
Experience Required: 6+ years

Sponsorship: U.S. Citizens, Green Card Holders, EAD Holders, and H-1B transfer candidates are encouraged to apply. We are unable to sponsor new H-1B visa petitions for this position.

Job Summary
We are seeking a Multi-Cloud Architect to design strategies, reference architectures, and platform capabilities that span multiple cloud providers — AWS, Azure, GCP, and selectively OCI — for enterprises operating on more than one cloud by deliberate choice. The role focuses on portability, abstraction layers, federated identity, cross-cloud networking, and platform offerings that hide cloud-specific complexity from product teams. The ideal candidate has architected meaningful multi-cloud capabilities, understands the trade-offs between portability and cloud-native depth, and brings strong opinions grounded in production experience.

Key Responsibilities
  • Define multi-cloud strategy, target-state architecture, and adoption guardrails across AWS, Azure, GCP, and OCI as relevant.
  • Design federated identity, SSO, and cross-cloud authorization patterns that let workloads and engineers move between providers without compromising on least-privilege, auditability, or operational simplicity.
  • Architect cross-cloud networking including transit hubs, private connectivity, and zero-trust patterns.
  • Establish reusable infrastructure-as-code patterns that abstract cloud-specific implementations where appropriate.
  • Define container, Kubernetes, and serverless strategies that work consistently across providers.
  • Design data architecture strategies for cross-cloud data movement, residency, and analytics.
  • Drive multi-cloud observability, security monitoring, and unified policy enforcement, designing approaches that work consistently across providers and avoid the complexity of fragmented per-cloud tooling stacks.
  • Establish FinOps practices that operate consistently across multiple cloud providers.
  • Lead disaster recovery and business continuity strategies that span clouds.
  • Partner with security architects on multi-cloud security models, KMS strategies, and key management.
  • Provide guidance to engineering teams on when to use cloud-agnostic versus cloud-native patterns.
  • Produce high-quality architecture artifacts — context diagrams, sequence diagrams, decision records, and reference designs — that capture key technical decisions clearly enough to be understood months or years later.
  • Engage with cloud providers and partners to evaluate roadmap alignment.
  • Stay current with multi-cloud platform and tooling developments, regularly review release notes and community discussions, and translate noteworthy advances into concrete recommendations and adoption proposals for the team.
Required Qualifications
  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science or a related field.
  • Eight or more years of experience in cloud architecture roles.
  • Hands-on architecture experience across at least two major cloud providers.
  • Deep understanding of cloud networking, identity, and security across multiple providers.
  • Strong experience with infrastructure-as-code and policy-as-code across clouds.
  • Experience designing federated identity and SSO across cloud platforms.
  • Solid understanding of Kubernetes, container platforms, and managed cloud services.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
  • Multiple cloud certifications across providers.
  • Track record of leading multi-cloud architecture initiatives.
Preferred Qualifications
  • Experience with abstraction platforms (Crossplane, Pulumi, Terraform CDK).
  • Familiarity with cloud-agnostic observability platforms.
  • Experience driving large-scale cloud-to-cloud migrations.
  • Exposure to regulated industries with multi-cloud mandates.
  • Public talks or writing on multi-cloud architecture.

jobs.description:
ACU is affiliated with the Fellowship of the Church of Christ. This position requires the employee to be a professing Christian and willing to support the Christian mission of ACU.

‌

The Talent Acquisition Specialist serves as a strategic, full-cycle recruiting partner responsible for attracting, assessing, and hiring mission-aligned talent for faculty, academic staff, adjuncts, students, temporary employees, leadership, and other employee populations. The position partners with hiring managers, academic leaders, and search committees to clarify workforce needs, develop sourcing strategies, facilitate consistent selection processes, and deliver a professional and welcoming candidate experience.

The position supports ACU's evolving centralized, shared-services talent acquisition model by strengthening recruiting governance, standardizing hiring practices, improving Workday Recruiting workflows, and developing sustainable candidate pipelines. The role also connects recruitment with workforce planning, employer branding, compensation and offer processes, onboarding, employee integration, and broader employee flourishing initiatives across the ACU system.

This position has the potential to be on-site in Abilene, Texas, or remote.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

1. Full-Cycle Recruitment and Hiring

  • Lead assigned searches from approved requisition through accepted offer and onboarding transition for faculty, academic, staff, adjunct, student, temporary, leadership, high-volume, hard-to-fill, and other positions.

  • Conduct intake meetings with hiring managers, academic leaders, and search committees to clarify position requirements, competencies, candidate profiles, sourcing strategies, timelines, and selection processes.

  • Create and manage requisitions, postings, approvals, candidate workflows, interview activity, dispositions, and offer documentation in Workday Recruiting.

  • Review applications and resumes against approved minimum and preferred qualifications, conduct structured phone or video screenings, and present qualified candidate slates with clear screening documentation.

  • Coordinate interviews, candidate communications, reference checks, background checks, employment verifications, and other required pre-employment activities.

  • Coordinate compensation and offer approvals with Talent Management and Total Rewards, and facilitate timely, professional offer communication and negotiation support.

  • Maintain timely communication with candidates and hiring stakeholders throughout the recruitment lifecycle.

2. Faculty, Academic, Staff, and Student Recruitment

  • Partner with Academic Affairs, deans, department chairs, and search committees on faculty, academic, adjunct, and other academic searches.

  • Support consistent search practices while respecting academic authority for evaluating credentials, discipline-specific qualifications, and academic selection decisions.

  • Support administrative, professional, operational, student, temporary, and other workforce recruitment across ACU divisions and locations.

  • Develop scalable recruiting approaches for recurring, high-volume, specialized, and difficult-to-fill positions.

  • Provide cross-functional recruiting coverage based on institutional priorities, workload, and business continuity needs.

3. Hiring Manager and Search Committee Partnership

  • Serve as a consultative recruiting partner to hiring managers and search committees throughout the hiring process.

  • Provide structured interview guides, evaluation tools, scorecards, and guidance on job-related candidate assessment and selection practices.

  • Assist departments with developing or updating position descriptions and translating workforce needs into clear qualifications and recruiting criteria.

  • Promote consistent hiring processes, approval requirements, documentation standards, and appropriate escalation of compliance, compensation, or selection concerns.

  • Build collaborative relationships across Human Resources, Academic Affairs, Finance, operational divisions, and campus leadership.

4. Talent Sourcing, Pipelines, and Employer Brand

  • Develop targeted sourcing strategies using professional networks, higher education resources, digital platforms, employee referrals, professional associations, churches, community organizations, and passive outreach.

  • Build and maintain talent pipelines for recurring, critical, leadership, and difficult-to-fill roles.

  • Represent ACU at selected job fairs, career events, professional gatherings, and recruiting activities.

  • Contribute to recruitment marketing, employment branding, and value-proposition initiatives that position ACU as a compelling, mission-centered employment destination.

  • Monitor labor-market conditions, sourcing effectiveness, and emerging talent gaps to inform recruiting and workforce-planning strategies.

5. Candidate Experience and Onboarding Partnership

  • Promote a candidate experience that reflects ACU’s Christian mission, institutional values, hospitality, professionalism, and commitment to employee flourishing.

  • Coordinate virtual and in-person recruiting activities and ensure candidates receive clear, timely, and respectful communication.

  • Facilitate a smooth transition from accepted offer to onboarding, orientation, integration, and employee-specific onboarding pathways.

  • Partner with HR Operations, onboarding and development leaders, Academic Affairs, and hiring departments to support effective new-hire transitions.

  • Identify and address candidate-experience gaps and recommend practical improvements.

6. Compliance, Documentation, and Hiring Governance

  • Apply university policies and established hiring requirements and support compliance with applicable federal and state employment laws.

  • Maintain complete, accurate, confidential, and auditable recruitment and selection records.

  • Promote consistent, job-related screening and selection practices and appropriate candidate disposition documentation.

  • Identify and escalate potential hiring, compensation, conflict-of-interest, records, or compliance concerns to the appropriate HR leader.

  • Support process standardization and governance across divisions, campuses, and employee populations.

7. Workday Recruiting and Systems Support

  • Use Workday Recruiting as the primary platform for requisition, candidate, interview, disposition, offer, and hiring workflow administration.

  • Support hiring managers and search committees in using Workday recruiting processes and employee or manager self-service practices.

  • Monitor workflows, data quality, approvals, and aging activity and resolve or escalate process issues.

  • Participate in Workday testing, optimization, reporting, automation, and system-enhancement initiatives affecting recruitment.

  • Maintain accurate candidate and recruiting data and support electronic records-management requirements.

8. Reporting, Workforce Planning, and Continuous Improvement

  • Monitor recruiting measures such as time-to-fill, requisition aging, candidate pipelines, source effectiveness, offer acceptance, and hiring activity.

  • Prepare recruiting dashboards, hiring reports, and workforce insights for HR and institutional leaders.

  • Identify recurring delays, process gaps, and opportunities to improve hiring quality, velocity, governance, and stakeholder experience.

  • Support workforce-planning discussions by identifying emerging hiring needs, labor-market trends, and talent risks.

  • Participate in talent acquisition projects, process improvement, policy development, cross-training, and business continuity planning.

  • Perform other duties as assigned that are consistent with the purpose and level of the position.

Supervisory Responsibilities

None. The position may coordinate search committees, recruiting vendors, temporary resources, career-event activities, or project teams without formal supervisory authority.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Communications, Organizational Leadership, Higher Education Administration, or a related field; equivalent relevant education and experience may be considered.

  • Three years of progressively responsible recruiting, talent acquisition, staffing, human resources, or related experience.

  • Experience managing multiple concurrent full-cycle recruitment processes.

About the team

The Agentic AI team at Zillow is at the forefront of transforming the real estate industry by helping millions of people use AI technologies to find their next home. About the role

Zillow is looking for a Principal Machine Learning Engineer on the Agentic AI team to develop advanced multimodal foundational technologies. They will be hands-on in prototyping ideas, evaluating, and deploying models to Zillow's highly scalable infrastructure platforms. They’ll be developing perception and language understanding, deep reasoning, and reinforcement learning to handle AI agent decision-making.

As a Principal Machine Learning Engineer on the Agentic AI team, you will:

  • Leverage frameworks like AgentSDK, and LangChain/LangGraph to design, prototype, and develop multi-agent systems that are capable of highly autonomous and context-aware interactions

  • Leverage advanced GenAI models including reasoning models, real-time voice API, etc, to build agentic prototypes and later on convert them into product-level agentic skills and deploy to users.

  • Remain on the cutting edge of agentic AI emerging paradigms, driving product innovation

  • Serve as the focal point for applied science projects, driving alignment on timelines, and prioritization

  • Continuously refine processes for experimentation, A/B testing, and production rollouts to balance rapid innovation with reliability and responsible deployment.

As a Principal Machine Learning Engineer, you are a roll-up-the-sleeves and get-it-done engineer who can marry state-of-the-art technology (i.e., LLM models, either from OpenAI or open source) with large-scale engineering. We are looking for someone who has:

  • Experience deploying and scaling AI services capable of handling hundreds of millions of daily interactions with high availability, low latency, and robust fault tolerance
